Either way, write the choice into the lease. A parking charge paid to you is rent, because rent is 'a payment to be made to the landlord under the rental agreement' (Iowa Code § 562A.6(10); `edu-fees-as-rent-ia`). So state the space and the charge at signing, and do not start or raise a parking charge during a fixed term: a rent increase may not take effect before the end of the term and needs 30 days' written notice (Iowa Code § 562A.13(5); `edu-rent-increase-notice-ia`). A parking rule adopted after the tenant signs binds the tenant only with reasonable notice and only if 'it does not work a substantial modification of the rental agreement' (Iowa Code § 562A.18(2)), so taking away an included space mid-term is risky. Use `assigned-parking-space` and `parking-ks-oh-ca` for the lease terms, and see `edu-towing-ia` for removing vehicles. City zoning codes may set parking requirements for buildings (Des Moines, Iowa City, Cedar Rapids and Ames among them). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Requiring Renter's Insurance in Iowa
bodyText:
Iowa has no statute on renter's insurance in a residential lease. Nothing bars you from requiring it, nothing makes you let the tenant pick the carrier, nothing regulates coverage you buy for the tenant, and nothing requires you to warn the tenant that your insurance does not cover the tenant's belongings. You may require renter's insurance as a lease term (Iowa Code § 562A.9(1)); use `tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`, which also tells the tenant your insurance does not cover the tenant's property.

Three cautions. First, do not add a clause saying you are never liable for the tenant's losses: an Iowa lease may not have the tenant agree 'to the exculpation or limitation of any liability of the other party arising under law' (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(d)).

Second, let the tenant choose the insurer. Iowa's ban on requiring a particular insurer is written for lenders and credit (Iowa Code § 507B.5), not leases, but naming one company invites a dispute and gains you nothing.

Third, the library offers no clause letting you buy coverage and bill the tenant. Any such charge would be rent (Iowa Code § 562A.6(10)), so it must be agreed at signing and could not be added during the term (Iowa Code § 562A.13(5)). If the tenant fails to keep required insurance, treat it as a lease breach and use the noncompliance notice (`edu-noncompliance-cure-ia`).

Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No State Landlord Insurance Mandate
bodyText: No Iowa statute requires a residential landlord to carry liability or property insurance, to show tenants proof of insurance, or to file insurance with the state. Cities with 15,000 or more people must run housing codes with 'a program for regular rental inspections, rental inspections upon receipt of complaints, and certification of inspected rental housing' (Iowa Code § 364.17(3)(a)), and a city may adopt stricter provisions (Iowa Code § 364.17(7)). Check your city's rental code and registration rules (Des Moines, Iowa City, Cedar Rapids and Ames among them) for any insurance condition. See `edu-rental-inspection-ia`. Your lender, a homeowners association or a housing program contract may also require coverage. Carrying liability and property insurance is prudent in any case: Iowa makes you liable for keeping the premises fit and the common areas safe (`edu-habitability-ia`), and a lease cannot shift that liability to the tenant (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(d)). Requiring the tenant to carry renter's insurance is a separate question (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`, `edu-no-renters-insurance-rules-ia`). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Insurance Claims Against a Tenant
bodyText: Iowa has no statute that protects a tenant from a claim for an accidental fire, and none that governs whether your insurer may sue the tenant after paying your claim. What the statutes do say: the tenant must 'Not deliberately or negligently destroy, deface, damage, impair or remove a part of the premises or knowingly permit a person to do so' (Iowa Code § 562A.17(6)), and you may recover damages for that breach (`edu-tenant-caused-damage-ia`, `tenant-caused-damage-ia`). A tenant is not liable under that duty for a fire that was nobody's fault. Iowa's standard fire policy lets your insurer 'require from the insured an assignment of all right of recovery against any party for loss to the extent that payment therefor is made by this company' (Iowa Code § 515.109(6)). Whether an Iowa landlord's insurer may use that to sue a negligent tenant, or whether the tenant is treated as protected by your policy, is a question for case law not searched for this library. Do not promise the tenant either answer. Two lease limits apply whatever the answer. A lease may not make the tenant 'indemnify the other party' (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(d)) for your own legal liability, and it may not take away the tenant's right to end the lease or pay reduced rent after a fire (Iowa Code § 562A.25; `edu-casualty-ia`). The practical course: require the tenant to carry renter's insurance with liability coverage (`tenants-property-insurance-ks-oh-ca`), keep your own coverage, and tell your insurer about the lease terms. The library offers no clause waiving or preserving your insurer's subrogation rights; if you want one, take advice and add your own. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Rent Reductions When a Subsidy Pays Part of the Rent
bodyText: Iowa has no rule on how a rent reduction for a damaged or unfit unit is split between the tenant's share and a housing subsidy. Iowa's reduction rules speak only of the tenant. After a fire or casualty, a tenant who stays may give up the unusable part, and 'the tenant's liability for rent is reduced in proportion to the diminution in the fair rental value of the dwelling unit' (Iowa Code § 562A.25(1)(b); `edu-casualty-ia`). If you deliberately or negligently fail to supply heat, water, hot water or essential services, the tenant may, after written notice, recover damages 'based upon the diminution in the fair rental value of the dwelling unit' (Iowa Code § 562A.23(1)(b)) or rent already paid for the period, 'reimbursed on a pro rata basis' (Iowa Code § 562A.23(1)(c)). In a nonpayment case the tenant may counterclaim, and the court may order rent paid into court (Iowa Code § 562A.24; `edu-tenant-repair-remedies-ia`). None of these says whether the reduction comes off the tenant's share, the subsidy, or both. Your housing assistance payments contract and the program's rules decide what happens to the subsidy payment; federal law may add duties in covered housing, not covered here. The cautious course: when a unit is damaged or a service fails, tell the housing authority promptly, fix the problem, and do not demand that the tenant make up any subsidy the housing authority withholds or abates until you have checked your contract. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Shutdown Rent Protection in Iowa
bodyText: Iowa has no law that delays rent or eviction for federal or state workers during a government shutdown or furlough. A tenant who misses rent because of a shutdown is treated like any other tenant who misses rent: the three-day notice and eviction process apply (`edu-nonpayment-notice-ia`, `edu-eviction-process-ia`). You may agree to a payment plan. If you do, put it in writing and say that you are not waiving the right to full rent, because 'Acceptance of performance by the tenant that varies from the terms of the rental agreement or rules subsequently adopted by the landlord constitutes a waiver of the landlord's right to terminate the rental agreement for that breach' (Iowa Code § 562A.30(1)). A temporary waiver for a set number of days works only if you give the tenant notice of the breach and of the waiver before the tenant relies on it (Iowa Code § 562A.30(2); `edu-waiver-by-acceptance-ia`). Servicemembers have separate protections (`edu-servicemember-ia`); federal law may add protections in some cases, not covered here. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Guarantors, Renewals and Iowa's Surety Statute
bodyText:
No Iowa statute says whether a lease guarantor stays liable after the original term ends, and none requires a guaranty to state a maximum or an end date. So say it in the guaranty. Use the guaranty clause (`guaranty-as`) and choose whether it covers renewals, extensions, month-to-month continuation and rent changes. For extra safety, have the guarantor sign each renewal.

The guaranty must be in writing and signed by the guarantor: a promise 'to answer for the debt, default, or miscarriage of another' (Iowa Code § 622.32(2)) cannot otherwise be proved.

Iowa also has an old surety statute. A person 'bound as surety for another for the payment of money' (Iowa Code § 540.1) who fears the principal 'is about to become insolvent or remove permanently from the state' (Iowa Code § 540.1) may, once a claim has accrued, demand in writing that you sue. If you refuse or neglect to sue 'for ten days after request, and does not permit the surety to do so' (Iowa Code § 540.2), the surety is discharged. No case read for this library says whether a lease guarantor counts as a surety under this statute.

The cautious course: if a guarantor sends you a written demand to sue the tenant, within ten days either file suit or let the guarantor sue in your name at the guarantor's cost, give the guarantor a true copy of the lease and the use of the original for the suit (Iowa Code § 540.2), and get legal advice. If you take any money from a guarantor as security, keep the total deposit within Iowa's two-months'-rent cap (Iowa Code § 562A.12(1); `edu-deposit-cap-ia`).

Do not add an attorney-fee promise to the guaranty: an Iowa lease may not provide that a party 'Agrees to pay the other party's attorney fees' (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(c)), and a guaranty written into the lease is safest without one.

Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Victim Address Confidentiality
bodyText: Iowa has no statute telling you how to handle the statement, police report or court order a tenant or applicant gives you about domestic abuse, sexual abuse or stalking, and none makes that paperwork confidential in your hands. Iowa does have an address confidentiality program, run by the Secretary of State, for victims of domestic abuse, sexual abuse, assault, stalking and human trafficking (Iowa Code ch. 9E), and parts of it bind any person, landlords included. If an applicant or tenant gives you a program designated address, accept it as their address: 'When a program participant presents the program participant's designated address to any person, that designated address shall be accepted as the address of the program participant' (Iowa Code § 9E.5(1)). Don't insist on another address that would show where the person lives (for example a current home address on an application) unless you could not provide the service without it (Iowa Code § 9E.5(1)). That section 'does not apply to documents or records relating to real property' (Iowa Code § 9E.5(6)), and no case read for this library says whether a lease or rental application is one; the cautious course is to honor the designated address anyway. Once a participant has told you in writing, on the Secretary of State's form, that they are in the program, you must not knowingly disclose their address except to someone who also lives, works or goes to school there, or with their written consent (Iowa Code § 9E.5(5)). Once a participant has told you in writing that they are in the program, you must not let their name be displayed at the protected address, for example on a mailbox, buzzer panel or lobby directory (Iowa Code § 9E.7(4)). The program does not stop you enforcing the lease (Iowa Code § 9E.7(6)). The Secretary of State is a participant's agent for service of process (Iowa Code § 9E.5(4)), so ask your attorney how to serve court papers on a participant. A person seeking a domestic abuse protective order may also use a shelter, post office box or other mailing address for utility and other services (Iowa Code § 236.10(1)). Cautious course for everything else: keep any statement, police report, court order or advocate's letter in a separate, secure file; use it only to manage the tenancy; and don't share it, or the tenant's whereabouts, with the person named as the abuser, other household members, screening services or reference callers unless the tenant agrees in writing or a court or law requires it. Federal law may add confidentiality duties in federally assisted housing; not covered here. See `edu-dv-eviction-protection-ia` (the protective steps that block a three-day termination), `edu-emergency-assistance-ia` and `edu-no-dv-termination-ia`. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Deposits When a Victim Leaves
bodyText: Iowa sets no special deposit rule for a tenant who leaves because of domestic abuse, sexual abuse or stalking, because Iowa gives victims no statutory right to end a lease early (`edu-no-dv-termination-ia`). The ordinary rule applies: within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you receive the tenant's mailing address or delivery instructions, return the deposit or give a written statement of the specific reason for keeping any part of it (Iowa Code § 562A.12(3)(a); `security-deposit-return-ia`). Iowa law doesn't say what happens to a single deposit when one co-tenant leaves and the others stay, or how it is divided among co-tenants. The statute speaks of a deposit held 'for the tenant, who is a party to the agreement' (Iowa Code § 562A.12(2)), and its clock starts at the end of the tenancy, which has not ended while the others remain. So if you agree to release a victim from the lease, put in the same signed agreement, with every tenant, how the deposit will be handled: either it stays as security for the continuing tenancy and is accounted for when that tenancy ends, or you account now for an agreed share. You may keep deposit money only for unpaid rent or other money due under the lease, restoring the unit beyond ordinary wear and tear, and some costs of regaining possession from a tenant who holds over in bad faith (Iowa Code § 562A.12(3)(a)). If your release agreement charges a fee, say whether it may come out of the deposit; otherwise bill it separately, and consider waiving it. Keeping a deposit in bad faith can cost punitive damages of up to twice the monthly rent on top of actual damages (Iowa Code § 562A.12(7); `edu-deposit-return-penalty-ia`). Federal law may add rules in federally assisted housing; not covered here. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Victim Lock-Change Statute
bodyText: Iowa has no statute giving a victim of domestic abuse, sexual abuse or stalking a right to have the locks changed, requiring you to change them, voiding a lease term about it, or saying who pays; Iowa has no general lock or rekeying statute either (`edu-no-security-device-rule-ia`). You may agree to a victim's request, and the cautious course is to change or re-key promptly when asked and keep a key for your own lawful entry (`edu-landlord-entry-ia`). Be careful when the person the victim fears is also a tenant. You may recover possession only through the courts or after abandonment or surrender (Iowa Code § 562A.33), and a tenant you unlawfully remove or exclude can recover possession, actual damages, punitive damages of up to twice the monthly rent and attorney fees (Iowa Code § 562A.26; `edu-self-help-eviction-ia`). So don't lock out a co-tenant on the victim's word alone. A court can exclude the abuser. A domestic abuse protective order may order 'That the defendant grant possession of the residence to the plaintiff to the exclusion of the defendant' (Iowa Code § 236.5(1)(b)(3)) or that the defendant stay away from the plaintiff's residence (Iowa Code § 236.5(1)(b)(4)), and temporary and emergency orders can do the same before a full hearing (Iowa Code § 236.4(2), Iowa Code § 236.6(1)). A sexual abuse protective order may order the defendant to stay away from the plaintiff's residence (Iowa Code § 236A.7(1)(b)); an elder abuse order may require a defendant who is a co-tenant to move out (Iowa Code § 235F.6(1)(a)); and a divorce court may order a spouse to vacate the home (Iowa Code § 598.33). If the victim gives you a copy of an order that grants the victim possession or bars the restrained person from the home, the cautious course is to change or re-key the locks for the victim, not to give the restrained person a key or let that person in while the order lasts, to keep a copy of the order with your records, and to call law enforcement if the person tries to enter. No Iowa statute says in so many words that you may or must do this. The order does not affect title to the property (Iowa Code § 236.5(6)), and no statute says what it does to the restrained person's lease or rent liability; take advice before changing that person's lease. Who pays is not set by statute. Iowa's crime victim compensation program can pay a victim up to $500 per residence to replace or install locks (Iowa Code § 915.86(14)), so you may point the victim to it. Follow your lease's key terms (`keys`), and consider waiving any charge. Federal law may add duties in federally assisted housing; not covered here. See `edu-no-dv-termination-ia` and `edu-dv-eviction-protection-ia`. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Protective-Order Citations in Iowa Tenant Law
bodyText: Iowa's landlord-tenant act refers to the protective-order laws in one place. A tenant avoids the three-day clear-and-present-danger termination if, among other steps, the tenant seeks 'a protective order, restraining order, order to vacate the homestead, or other similar relief pursuant to chapter 235F, 236, 598, 664A, or 915, or any other applicable provision' (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(3)(a)(1)); the manufactured home community act uses the same words (Iowa Code § 562B.25A(3)(a)(1)). None of those chapters has moved: elder abuse orders (Iowa Code ch. 235F), domestic abuse protective orders (Iowa Code ch. 236), orders to vacate the home pending a divorce (Iowa Code § 598.33), criminal no-contact orders (Iowa Code ch. 664A) and orders protecting crime victims and witnesses from harassment (Iowa Code § 915.22) are all where the act points. One gap: since 2017, sexual abuse protective orders have had their own chapter (Iowa Code ch. 236A), which the list does not name. Such an order is still covered by the words 'any other applicable provision' (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(3)(a)(1)), so treat a tenant who sought one the same way. Two 2026 changes, effective July 1, 2026: a peace officer may now file an emergency domestic abuse petition for a person in present danger who asks (2026 Iowa Acts ch. 1080, § 1; Iowa Code § 236.6), and after a conviction for listed sexual offenses a sexual abuse order of protection may last beyond the usual one year, up to the victim's lifetime (2026 Iowa Acts ch. 1079, § 3; Iowa Code § 236A.7(3)). So an order a tenant shows you may be more than a year old and still in force; go by the expiry the order itself states. Your three-day notice must set out the language of subsection 3 of the clear-and-present-danger statute (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(1)): copy the statute's current words rather than an old form. See `edu-dv-eviction-protection-ia`, `edu-clear-present-danger-ia` and, for orders that exclude an abuser from the home, `edu-no-dv-lockchange-ia`.

title: Proof a Victim Must Give You
bodyText: Iowa has one document rule for victims, in the clear-and-present-danger statute. A tenant avoids a three-day termination for another person's dangerous activity by taking one of three steps against that person: seeking a protective, restraining, no-contact or similar order; reporting the activity to law enforcement or the county attorney to start a criminal case; or writing the person a no-trespass letter and sending a copy to law enforcement (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(3)(a)). The tenant must also give you 'written proof to the landlord, prior to the commencement of a suit against the tenant' (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(3)(b)) that the step was taken. The statute does not list which documents count, does not require a particular form, and sets no limit on how old the document may be; the only deadline is that the proof must reach you before the eviction suit is started. A copy of the petition or order, a police or county attorney report or case number, or the letter with proof that a copy went to law enforcement all fit the words. A letter works only once against the same person: if, after a letter alone, that person again conducts activities causing a clear and present danger, the tenant must seek an order or report to law enforcement (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(3)(a)(3)). Iowa's other victim protection, the right to call police or emergency help without penalty (Iowa Code § 562A.27B; `edu-emergency-assistance-ia`), requires no documents, and Iowa has no victim lease-termination right whose paperwork you could ask for (`edu-no-dv-termination-ia`). The address confidentiality program works by the participant's own written notice on the Secretary of State's form (`edu-dv-confidentiality-ia`). Cautious course: accept any written proof that reasonably shows one of the three steps was taken, check what you have received before you file, don't demand a particular document, and keep what you receive confidential (`edu-dv-confidentiality-ia`). See `edu-dv-eviction-protection-ia` and `edu-dv-protection-order-citations-ia`. Federal law may add documentation rules in federally assisted housing; not covered here. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: When an Iowa Tenant May End a Lease Early
No Early Exit for Age, Illness or Care
bodyText: Iowa has no statute letting a tenant end a lease early because of age, illness, disability or a move into a nursing home, assisted living or other care, and no statute that ends a tenancy when a tenant or landlord becomes incapacitated. The lease controls. A fixed-term lease runs to its end date, and a month-to-month or week-to-week tenancy ends on ordinary written notice (`edu-end-of-term-ia`, `periodic-tenancy-notice-ia`). Iowa's general tenancy-at-will rule also requires 30 days' written notice to end the tenancy (or the rent interval, if shorter) and says nothing about incapacity (Iowa Code § 562.4). Once the tenant has moved into a care facility, the stay there is not a tenancy under Iowa's landlord-tenant act, which does not govern 'Residence at an institution, public or private, if incidental to detention or the provision of medical, geriatric, educational, counseling, religious, or similar service' (Iowa Code § 562A.5(1)). Fair housing law still applies: a request to end a lease early because of a disability can be a request for a reasonable accommodation, so consider it on its facts (`edu-fair-housing-ia`). Cautious course: if a tenant or the tenant's family asks to end the lease because the tenant must move into care, consider agreeing to a written early termination, deal with an agent under a power of attorney or a court-appointed guardian or conservator for a tenant who cannot act, and in any case make reasonable efforts to re-rent before claiming rent for the rest of the term (Iowa Code § 562A.29(3); `edu-abandonment-mitigation-ia`). See `edu-statutory-early-termination-ia` for the exits Iowa does give, and `edu-no-tenant-death-rule-ia` if the tenant dies. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Way Out of the Lease Over Repair Costs
bodyText: No Iowa statute lets you, or the tenant, end a lease because a needed repair would cost too much compared with the rent or the value of the property. Your repair duty has no cost ceiling: you must 'Make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition' (Iowa Code § 562A.15(1)(a)(2)), and a lease can't waive that duty (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a); `edu-habitability-ia`), apart from a lease of a single-family home on land assessed as agricultural land in an unincorporated area; the written tenant repair agreements Iowa Code § 562A.15(2) and Iowa Code § 562A.15(3) allow can move specified repairs to the tenant but do not remove the duty (`maintenance-allocation-ia`). Cost matters in only two narrow ways. First, if you show you used due diligence and effort and the failure to fix was due to circumstances reasonably beyond your control, you avoid the tenant's damages claim, though not the tenant's right to end the lease after a seven-day notice (Iowa Code § 562A.21(2); `edu-tenant-repair-remedies-ia`). Second, if bringing the unit up to the building or housing code would take alteration, remodeling or demolition that would effectively deprive the tenant of its use, you may bring an action for possession even though the tenant recently complained, but that does not release you from the tenant's damages claim (Iowa Code § 562A.36(3)(c); `edu-retaliation-ia`). Neither is a right to end a fixed-term lease early. Your ways out are the ordinary ones: the lease ends on its end date, a periodic tenancy ends on written notice (`edu-end-of-term-ia`), or you and the tenant agree in writing to end it, for example with relocation help or a rent refund. After fire or casualty the statute gives only the tenant a right to end the lease (Iowa Code § 562A.25; `edu-casualty-ia`); the library offers an optional clause giving you a narrow casualty termination right (`casualty-termination-ia`). It offers no repair-cost termination clause, because a clause letting you walk away from repairs you owe risks being an unenforceable waiver of the tenant's rights, with a penalty if used knowingly (Iowa Code § 562A.11(3)). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Environmental-Event Termination Right
bodyText: Iowa gives neither you nor the tenant a statutory right to end a lease because a flood, contamination, sewer failure, smoke, a public health emergency, a disaster declaration or a government order makes the home unfit or unlawful to occupy. The one event-driven rule belongs to the tenant: if the unit is damaged or destroyed 'by fire or casualty to an extent that enjoyment of the dwelling unit is substantially impaired' (Iowa Code § 562A.25(1)), the tenant may move out at once and give written notice within 14 days, ending the lease on the move-out date, or, if staying is lawful, stop using the unusable part and pay reduced rent (`edu-casualty-ia`). The statute does not define casualty. Physical damage from a flood or storm is likely to count, but whether contamination or a government order without physical damage counts is not settled; when in doubt, treat a tenant's notice as effective rather than fight it. Otherwise your duties continue: you must comply with building and housing codes and keep the unit fit (Iowa Code § 562A.15(1)(a)), and a tenant may end the lease on a seven-day notice if you don't (Iowa Code § 562A.21(1); `edu-statutory-early-termination-ia`). The library's only landlord event right for Iowa is the optional fire-or-casualty clause (`casualty-termination-ia`). It offers no wider environmental-event termination clause for you, because a clause letting you end the lease after a non-casualty event would end your repair duty for the rest of the term, which a court could treat as an unenforceable waiver of the tenant's rights (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a)). If you want one, take advice and add your own clause. If a tenant does not leave after a lease ends, regain possession only through the courts (Iowa Code § 562A.33; `edu-self-help-eviction-ia`). City housing codes and orders (Des Moines, Iowa City, Cedar Rapids, Ames and others; `edu-rental-inspection-ia`) may require occupants to leave an unsafe building; follow them. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here. The waiver bar in Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a) does not apply to a lease of a single-family residence on land assessed as agricultural land and located in an unincorporated area.

title: When Iowa Stops or Redirects Rent
bodyText: No Iowa statute forbids you to demand or collect rent because a unit has been cited for code violations, placarded or declared unfit, as some states do. Rent is due without any demand: 'Rent shall be payable without demand or notice at the time and place agreed upon by the parties' (Iowa Code § 562A.9(3)). But Iowa stops, reduces or redirects rent in these cases: (1) if you fail to deliver possession at the start of the term, 'rent abates until possession is delivered' (Iowa Code § 562A.22(1)); (2) after fire or casualty, a tenant who ends the lease owes rent only to the date of the casualty, and a tenant who stays in the usable part pays reduced rent (Iowa Code § 562A.25); (3) if you deliberately or negligently fail to supply heat, running water, hot water or essential services, the tenant may, after written notice, buy them and deduct the cost from rent, or recover rent already paid for that period (Iowa Code § 562A.23(1)); (4) a tenant who gave you notice at least seven days before the rent due date and then, in good faith and before receiving your written notice to terminate for nonpayment, had a breach corrected that cost no more than one month's rent may deduct the cost, and it is a defense to an eviction for nonpayment (Iowa Code § 562A.27(4); `edu-tenant-repair-remedies-ia`); (5) in a nonpayment case the tenant may counterclaim, the court may order rent paid into court, and if no rent remains due the tenant keeps possession (Iowa Code § 562A.24(1); `edu-rent-into-court-ia`); (6) when a court appoints a receiver to abate a public nuisance at abandoned or neglected property, it may empower the receiver to collect the rents and evict tenants (Iowa Code § 657A.6(1)), so rent goes to the receiver, not to you; (7) you may not retaliate by raising rent after a protected complaint (Iowa Code § 562A.36(1); `edu-retaliation-ia`); and (8) you may not end a servicemember's lease for nonpayment during military service where the rent is under $1,200 a month except through a court (Iowa Code § 29A.101(1); `edu-servicemember-ia`). Before ending a tenancy for nonpayment you must give the written three-day notice (Iowa Code § 562A.27(2); `edu-nonpayment-notice-ia`), and federal law may require 30 days' notice to vacate for covered properties (`edu-cares-act-notice`). Cautious course: fix code violations promptly, and don't rent, or collect rent for, a unit a city has ordered vacated (`edu-rental-inspection-ia`). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Your Remedies When a Tenancy Ends
bodyText: Your remedies when an Iowa tenancy ends or the tenant defaults: (1) Possession only through the courts, by a forcible entry and detainer action, never by lockout, removing belongings or cutting services (Iowa Code § 562A.33; `edu-eviction-process-ia`, `edu-self-help-eviction-ia`). (2) Possession and money together: once the lease is terminated you 'may have a claim for possession and for rent and a separate claim for actual damages for breach of the rental agreement and reasonable attorney fees as provided in section 562A.27' (Iowa Code § 562A.32). Attorney fees come only where a statute allows them, for example for a tenant's willful noncompliance (Iowa Code § 562A.27(3); `edu-attorney-fees-ia`). The eviction may be filed together only with a claim for rent or for the recovery the statute lists, such as your damages after termination; the court treats them as separate cases with one filing fee, and the tenant can't counterclaim in the eviction itself (Iowa Code § 648.19). In a nonpayment case the tenant may counterclaim in the rent case, and the court may order rent paid into court (Iowa Code § 562A.24; `edu-rent-into-court-ia`). (3) Damages without ending the lease: you may recover damages and get an injunction for the tenant's noncompliance while the lease continues, unless the tenant shows due diligence and circumstances beyond their control (Iowa Code § 562A.27(3)). (4) Holdover: possession, plus actual damages and attorney fees for a willful, bad-faith holdover (Iowa Code § 562A.34(4); `edu-holdover-ia`). (5) A tenant who leaves early: you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent, and the lease ends when a new tenancy begins or, if you don't try or you accept the surrender, when you learn of the abandonment (Iowa Code § 562A.29(3); `edu-abandonment-mitigation-ia`). No Iowa statute allows or bars a clause making all rent for the rest of the term due at once (acceleration); because of the mitigation duty and the penalty doctrine, don't rely on one without advice (`edu-no-liquidated-damages-rule-ia`). (6) The deposit may be applied to unpaid rent and damage as the deposit statute allows (Iowa Code § 562A.12(3); `security-deposit-use-ia`). Which court: an eviction on the usual grounds may be brought in small claims or in district court in the county where the property is (Iowa Code § 631.1(2), Iowa Code § 648.5(1)). A money claim of $6,500 or less, apart from interest and costs, is a small claim (Iowa Code § 631.1(1)(b)); larger claims go to district court. Accepting performance from the tenant that varies from the lease waives your right to terminate for that breach (Iowa Code § 562A.30; `edu-waiver-by-acceptance-ia`), and 30 days' peaceable possession after the claim arises with your knowledge bars the eviction (Iowa Code § 648.18). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Hardship Stay of Evictions
bodyText: Iowa has no hardship stay: no statute lets a court delay an eviction because moving out would be hard on the tenant or the tenant's family, or because of the season. The delays Iowa does have are these. (1) The court sets the hearing no later than 8 days after filing, or up to 15 days if you ask or agree (Iowa Code § 648.5(1)). If the hearing would be held fewer than three days after service, or the tenant appears without proper service, the court must tell the tenant of the right to a continuance and grant one on request (Iowa Code § 648.5(5)). (2) In a case filed in district court rather than small claims, if there is a genuine issue of material fact the court continues the case for an evidentiary hearing (Iowa Code § 648.5(7)). (3) After judgment, the order for removal issues within three days (Iowa Code § 648.22) and can be carried out only in the daytime (Iowa Code § 648.20). (4) In small claims, an appeal stops enforcement only if the appealing party files an appeal bond with surety approved by the clerk, in the sum the judgment specifies (Iowa Code § 631.13(2); `edu-possession-bond-ia`). (5) For a servicemember or dependents, the court may stay the case for up to three months unless military service has not materially affected the ability to pay (Iowa Code § 29A.101(2); `edu-servicemember-ia`). In a nonpayment case the tenant's counterclaim and any order to pay rent into court can also change the outcome (Iowa Code § 562A.24; `edu-rent-into-court-ia`). No Iowa statute authorizes or forbids a local eviction moratorium. Federal law (for example a bankruptcy filing or the CARES Act notice, `edu-cares-act-notice`) may add delays; not covered here. See `edu-eviction-process-ia`. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Who Can Receive Eviction Papers
bodyText: Who may receive Iowa eviction papers is set by statute. The original notice in a forcible entry and detainer case must be served by one or more of three methods: (1) delivery shown by an acknowledgment signed and dated by a resident of the premises who is at least 18, which counts as notice to all tenants and residents; (2) personal service under the Iowa Rules of Civil Procedure; or (3) only after two failed attempts by (1) or (2), posting on the primary entrance door plus mailing by both regular and certified mail (Iowa Code § 648.5(2)). Each method must be completed at least three days before the hearing; after posting and mailing, file an affidavit with copies of what you posted and mailed (Iowa Code § 648.5(4)); and no default judgment may be entered without proper service (Iowa Code § 648.5(6)). The three-day notice to quit uses the same three methods, without the two-attempt condition (Iowa Code § 648.3(2)), and notices under the landlord-tenant act have their own list (Iowa Code § 562A.29A; `edu-notice-service-ia`). No Iowa statute provides for a person named in the lease to accept eviction papers for the tenant. Because an acknowledgment signed by any adult resident already reaches every tenant, the library offers no such clause; whether one would work under the civil procedure rules was not checked. Use the lease to fix where ordinary notices go instead (`notices`). Your own side: you must disclose in writing, at or before the start of the tenancy, the name and address of a person authorized to receive service of process for the owner, and anyone who fails to do so becomes an agent for service (Iowa Code § 562A.13; `landlord-disclosure-ia`). Address confidentiality participants: the Secretary of State is the participant's agent for service of process, forwards papers by certified mail within three days, and the date of service is the date the participant accepts or rejects them (Iowa Code § 9E.5(4)). No statute says how that fits the eviction hearing timetable or whether you may still serve at the rental unit. If you know a tenant is a participant, ask your attorney or the court before filing, and keep the tenant's address out of anything that doesn't need it (`edu-dv-confidentiality-ia`). See `edu-eviction-process-ia`. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Possession Bond in Iowa
bodyText: Iowa has no end-of-term possession bond, no bond a tenant must post to stay in the home while an eviction is pending, and no bond you post to get possession early. A lease bond backed by a confessed judgment is barred outright: an Iowa lease may not authorize 'a person to confess judgment on a claim arising out of the rental agreement' (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(b); `edu-confession-of-judgment-ia`). The one bond in an eviction comes after judgment in small claims: an appeal stops enforcement only if the appealing party files 'an appeal bond with surety approved by the clerk, in the sum specified in the judgment' (Iowa Code § 631.13(2)). Without that bond the removal order can issue within three days of judgment even while an appeal is pending (Iowa Code § 648.22). For an eviction decided in district court rather than small claims, appeal and stay bonds are governed by the appellate court rules. In a nonpayment case the court may instead order the tenant to pay rent into court while the case goes on; that is not a bond (Iowa Code § 562A.24; `edu-rent-into-court-ia`). A lease clause requiring the tenant to post a bond or other security before defending an eviction would risk being an unenforceable waiver of the tenant's rights (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a)); the security a lease may take is the deposit, capped at two months' rent (`edu-deposit-cap-ia`). See `edu-eviction-process-ia` and `edu-no-eviction-hardship-stay-ia`. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here. The waiver bar in Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a) does not apply to a lease of a single-family residence on land assessed as agricultural land and located in an unincorporated area.

title: Paying to Stop an Eviction
bodyText: Iowa gives a tenant a chance to pay before the tenancy ends, but no statutory right to redeem it afterwards. After your written three-day notice of nonpayment, a tenant who pays the rent within the three days keeps the tenancy; if not, you may terminate and file for eviction without a separate notice to quit (Iowa Code § 562A.27(2), Iowa Code § 648.3(1); `edu-nonpayment-notice-ia`). Other breaches carry a seven-day chance to cure (Iowa Code § 562A.27(1); `edu-noncompliance-cure-ia`). Once the tenancy has ended, no Iowa statute lets the tenant reinstate it by paying the arrears before the hearing, judgment or removal, and none requires you to accept such a payment or limits how many times you may. Two rules still matter. First, if you accept performance that varies from the lease, such as late or partial rent, you waive the right to terminate for that breach (Iowa Code § 562A.30(1); `edu-waiver-by-acceptance-ia`). The only statutory way to accept without waiving is a temporary waiver for a set number of days, with notice of the breach and the waiver given before the tenant relies on it (Iowa Code § 562A.30(2)); Iowa prescribes no reservation wording for receipts. Whether taking money after you have terminated, while an eviction is pending, revives the tenancy is a matter of case law; the cautious course is not to accept rent after termination unless you mean to continue the tenancy, or to put any agreement to dismiss the case in writing. Second, in a nonpayment eviction the tenant may counterclaim, the court may order rent paid into court, and if no rent remains due after the counterclaim the tenant keeps possession (Iowa Code § 562A.24(1); `edu-rent-into-court-ia`). No Iowa statute deals with rent paid for the tenant by a charity or government agency; treat it like any other payment for the waiver rule. Servicemembers have extra protection (`edu-servicemember-ia`), and federal rules may apply in subsidized housing; not covered here. See `edu-forfeiture-redemption-ia`. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Forfeiture of a Lease and Relief From It
bodyText: Iowa has no statute on relief from forfeiture of a lease, and none that lets a tenant undo a termination by paying or curing after the tenancy has ended. What Iowa has instead: (1) Chances to cure before the tenancy ends: three days to pay rent after your written notice, and seven days to remedy most other breaches, with no second chance for the same breach within six months and none for a clear and present danger (Iowa Code § 562A.27(1)-(2), Iowa Code § 562A.27A; `edu-redemption-ia`, `edu-noncompliance-cure-ia`, `edu-clear-present-danger-ia`). (2) No forfeiture by re-entry: whatever the lease says, you may recover possession only through a court action, or after abandonment or surrender (Iowa Code § 562A.33; `edu-self-help-eviction-ia`). The eviction is 'tried as an equitable action' (Iowa Code § 648.5(1)), and the general principles of law and equity supplement the landlord-tenant act (Iowa Code § 562A.3), but whether an Iowa court may relieve a tenant from a forfeiture is a matter of case law, not covered here. (3) Waiver: accepting performance that varies from the lease waives your right to terminate for that breach (Iowa Code § 562A.30; `edu-waiver-by-acceptance-ia`). (4) Waste: an older general statute lets the owner of the reversion who sues a tenant for waste obtain 'Judgment of forfeiture and eviction' when the damages recovered exceed two-thirds of the value of the tenant's interest (Iowa Code § 658.2), and makes a tenant for life or years who commits waste liable for three times the damages (Iowa Code § 658.1A). How those rules sit alongside the landlord-tenant act's own damage remedies is not settled by statute; for an ordinary residential tenancy use the act's notice and damage remedies (`tenant-caused-damage-ia`, `edu-tenant-caused-damage-ia`) and take advice before suing for waste. See `edu-landlord-remedies-termination-ia`. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Late-Benefit Eviction Defense
bodyText: Iowa has no statute giving a tenant a defense, a continuance or reinstatement because a Social Security check, another public benefit or a housing-subsidy payment arrived late. A tenant who falls behind for that reason gets the same written three-day notice and can be evicted like any other (Iowa Code § 562A.27(2); `edu-nonpayment-notice-ia`). The tenant still has the general protections: paying within the three days ends the matter, and accepting a late payment can waive your right to terminate for that breach (`edu-redemption-ia`, `edu-waiver-by-acceptance-ia`); a servicemember's rent default gets extra protection (`edu-servicemember-ia`). Two related rules. A municipal housing agency may not refuse to house an otherwise eligible person merely because the person receives public assistance, such as supplemental security income, unemployment compensation or Social Security (Iowa Code § 403A.23). And when you collect a money judgment, a debtor's 'social security benefit, unemployment compensation, or any public assistance benefit' (Iowa Code § 627.6(8)(a)) is exempt from execution, so you can't garnish or levy on it. Iowa law does not otherwise bar refusing a tenant because of a voucher or source of income (`edu-source-of-income-ia`). In subsidized housing the program's own federal rules and contracts may require notices or limit eviction when the agency's share is late; check them (`edu-voucher-tenancy-addendum`). Cautious course: if you know a late benefit or subsidy payment is the cause, a short written temporary waiver can keep the tenancy without losing your rights (Iowa Code § 562A.30(2)). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Cold-Weather Vacating Notice Rule
bodyText: Iowa has no statute requiring a tenant to warn you before vacating or leaving the unit in cold weather, and no seasonal rule like Minnesota's. What Iowa does allow is a lease term requiring notice of an extended absence: 'The rental agreement may require that the tenant notify the landlord of an anticipated extended absence from the premises not later than the first day of the extended absence' (Iowa Code § 562A.20). A tenant who willfully fails to give that notice owes your actual damages, such as frozen-pipe repairs, and during an absence of more than 14 days you may enter at reasonably necessary times (Iowa Code § 562A.29(1)-(2)). The library's extended-absence clause (`extended-absence-notice-ks`, which applies to Iowa) uses that right; it already covers a winter absence, so no separate cold-weather clause is offered. A tenant who moves out for good before the term ends has abandoned the unit; you must make reasonable efforts to re-rent (Iowa Code § 562A.29(3); `edu-abandonment-mitigation-ia`). Tenants must use the heating and plumbing in a reasonable manner (Iowa Code § 562A.17(5)), and the library's utility clause keeps them from cutting off services during the term (`utility-service-continuity`). Utility rules protect occupants, not landlords, in winter: a gas or electric utility may not disconnect a certified low-income household from November 1 through April 1 (Iowa Code § 476.20(3)); it may not disconnect a home whose only heat depends on that service when the temperature or 24-hour forecast is 20 degrees Fahrenheit or colder; and when it can't reach a tenant it must try to contact you, as landlord, and tell you the disconnection date at least 48 hours ahead (Iowa Admin. Code r. 199-20.4(14); gas rules are similar, Iowa Admin. Code r. 199-19.4(14)). If you get such a call about a unit that may be empty, check on it promptly. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Rule on Extra Terms in Move-Out Notices
bodyText: Iowa has no statute on move-out notice forms that add terms, and none that bars work on a unit while a notice to vacate is running. Iowa's notice statutes say who may end a tenancy, how much notice is due and how a notice is served (`periodic-tenancy-notice-ia`, `edu-end-of-term-ia`, `edu-notice-service-ia`); they say nothing about extra terms. Keep a notice to the facts it needs: the termination date and, for a tenant's form, a forwarding address. Put anything new, such as a cleaning charge, a release or a changed move-out date, in a separate agreement both of you sign. Neither a notice form nor that agreement may take away the tenant's rights under the landlord-tenant act: a rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant 'Agrees to waive or to forego rights or remedies under this chapter' (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a)) (except a lease of a single-family home on land assessed as agricultural land in an unincorporated area), and a court may refuse to enforce a settlement waiving a right under the act that was unconscionable when made (Iowa Code § 562A.7(1)(b)). While the notice runs, every duty you had continues until the tenancy ends. You must still 'Make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition' (Iowa Code § 562A.15(1)(a)(2); `edu-habitability-ia`). Cutting off electric, gas, water or another essential service lets the tenant recover possession or end the lease and recover actual damages, punitive damages of up to twice the monthly rent and attorney fees (Iowa Code § 562A.26). So schedule renovation for after the unit is empty. If complying with a housing code itself needs alteration, remodeling or demolition that would deprive the tenant of the unit, you may bring an action for possession even after a code complaint, but 'The maintenance of the action does not release the landlord from liability under section 562A.21, subsection 2' (Iowa Code § 562A.36(3)(c); `edu-retaliation-ia`). A tenant who serves notice of intention to quit at a named time and then holds over owes double the rental value for the holdover (Iowa Code § 562.2; `edu-holdover-ia`). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Ending a Lease to Move In: No Iowa Statute
bodyText:
No Iowa statute gives you a right to end a lease so that you or a relative can move in, and none limits that reason or sets a period you must live in the unit afterwards. Iowa has no just-cause eviction rule (`edu-no-good-cause-notice-ia`), so a month-to-month or week-to-week tenancy can be ended for this reason, or for none, on the ordinary notice (`periodic-tenancy-notice-ia`), and a fixed term can be ended at its end (`edu-end-of-term-ia`).

During a fixed term a silent lease gives you no early exit. If you want one, the lease must reserve it: Iowa lets the lease include 'terms and conditions not prohibited by this chapter or other rule of law including rent, term of the agreement' (Iowa Code § 562A.9(1)), and the library's optional Owner Occupancy clause (`owner-occupancy-termination-ar`) does that for a fixed term on written notice of at least the days you choose (not less than 30) to the end of a monthly rental period.

Serve that notice by a method the termination-notice statute allows (signed acknowledgment, personal service, or posting plus regular and certified mail; Iowa Code § 562A.29A(1)), even though the statute may not strictly require it for a notice the lease creates.

Two limits. A landlord 'may not retaliate by increasing rent or decreasing services or by bringing or threatening to bring an action for possession after' (Iowa Code § 562A.36(1)) a tenant's code complaint, repair complaint or tenant-union activity, and a good-faith complaint in the year before raises a presumption of retaliation (Iowa Code § 562A.36(2); `edu-retaliation-ia`); be ready to show the move-in is real. And a tenant who does not leave must be removed through the court, after a three days' notice to quit (Iowa Code § 648.3(1); `edu-eviction-process-ia`, `edu-self-help-eviction-ia`).

Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Good-Cause Eviction Law or Notice
bodyText:
Iowa has no good-cause or just-cause eviction law, so there is no state notice telling tenants whether such a law covers them and nothing to put in the lease about it. A fixed term ends at its end and a periodic tenancy ends on proper notice, without a stated reason (`edu-for-cause-eviction-ia`, `edu-end-of-term-ia`, `periodic-tenancy-notice-ia`).

Reasons matter only where a statute makes them matter. A notice ending the lease for the tenant's breach must state the breach (seven-day notice, Iowa Code § 562A.27(1); three-day nonpayment notice, Iowa Code § 562A.27(2); `edu-noncompliance-cure-ia`, `edu-nonpayment-notice-ia`). You may not end or refuse to renew a tenancy in retaliation for code complaints, repair complaints or tenant organizing (Iowa Code § 562A.36; `edu-retaliation-ia`), or because someone summoned police or emergency help; the emergency-assistance statute 'does not prohibit a landlord from terminating, evicting, or refusing to renew a tenancy or rental agreement when such action is premised upon grounds other than' (Iowa Code § 562A.27B(1)(f)) that call (`edu-emergency-assistance-ia`).

A municipal housing agency may give a thirty-day termination notice for a federal public housing eligibility violation (Iowa Code § 562A.27(5)). In a Housing Choice Voucher tenancy, federal rules limit ending the tenancy during the term to listed grounds (`edu-voucher-tenancy-addendum`).

Some Iowa cities, such as Des Moines, Iowa City, Cedar Rapids and Ames, run their own rental codes; check local rules.

Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Automatic Renewal Clauses in Iowa
bodyText:
No Iowa statute governs automatic-renewal clauses in residential leases. Iowa bans them only in fitness-club contracts (Iowa Code § 552.8), has no general consumer auto-renewal law, requires no reminder notice before a lease renews, and does not limit how early you may ask a tenant to commit to a renewal. So a renewal clause is a term you may agree with the tenant (Iowa Code § 562A.9(1)), and the library offers one: `automatic-renewal-ia`.

Three statutes shape it. First, either party 'may terminate a tenancy having a term longer than month-to-month by a written notice given to the other at least thirty days prior to the end of the first or subsequent term of the tenancy specified in the notice' (Iowa Code § 562A.34(3)), so a notice of non-renewal shorter than 30 days does not work. Whether a lease may make a tenant give more than 30 days is not settled; a court could read a longer period as a waiver of the tenant's statutory right, which an Iowa lease may not contain (Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a)). The library's clause therefore lets you choose your own notice period (at least 30 days) but holds the tenant to 30.

Second, a rent increase needs written notice to each tenant at least 30 days before it takes effect and cannot take effect before the current term ends (Iowa Code § 562A.13(5); `edu-rent-increase-notice-ia`).

Third, without a renewal clause a written lease that fixes its end date ends then (Iowa Code § 562.6), though serving a 30-day notice is still the cautious course (`edu-end-of-term-ia`); if you then let the tenant stay and accept rent, the tenancy runs month to month (Iowa Code § 562A.34(4), Iowa Code § 562A.9(5); `holdover-ia`).

Serve your notice of non-renewal by a method allowed for termination notices (Iowa Code § 562A.29A(1); `edu-notice-service-ia`).

Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here. The waiver bar in Iowa Code § 562A.11(1)(a) does not apply to a lease of a single-family residence on land assessed as agricultural land and located in an unincorporated area.

title: Tenancies at Will in Iowa
bodyText: Iowa still has a tenancy-at-will statute, in its general landlord-tenant chapter: 'A person in the possession of real estate, with the assent of the owner, is presumed to be a tenant at will until the contrary is shown' (Iowa Code § 562.4), and either side must serve thirty days' written notice on the other before the tenancy ends (Iowa Code § 562.4). If rent is payable at intervals shorter than thirty days, the notice need not be longer than the interval (Iowa Code § 562.4). For an ordinary residential rental, the landlord-tenant act gives the more specific rule: a rental with no definite term is week-to-week for a roomer who pays weekly rent and month-to-month in every other case (Iowa Code § 562A.9(5)), ended by written notice at least ten days before the termination date (week-to-week) or at least thirty days before the periodic rental date named in the notice (month-to-month) (Iowa Code § 562A.34(1)-(2); `periodic-tenancy-notice-ia`). The act's rules supplement and displace older law only where they speak (Iowa Code § 562A.3), and no Iowa decision reconciling the two was read for this library, so give a notice that meets both: in writing, at least thirty days before a rental due date (at least ten days for a weekly roomer), served by signed acknowledgment, personal service, or posting plus regular and certified mail (Iowa Code § 562A.29A(1)). The at-will statute matters most where the act does not apply, for example a caretaker whose right to live there depends on the job, or an occupant under a contract of sale (Iowa Code § 562A.5; `edu-scope-ia`). For nonpayment by a tenant at will, the three-day notice is enough: 'no notice of the termination of the tenancy other than the three-day notice need be given before beginning the action' (Iowa Code § 648.4); see `edu-nonpayment-notice-ia`. Iowa's Code does not use the term tenancy by sufferance. A tenant who stays after the tenancy ends without your consent is a holdover (Iowa Code § 648.1(2), Iowa Code § 562A.34(4); `edu-holdover-ia`), and a person who never had your assent is not presumed a tenant (`edu-no-squatter-statute-ia`). To avoid an uncertain arrangement, use a signed written lease that states its term. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Seasonal Tenancy Category in Iowa
bodyText: Iowa has no seasonal-tenancy category. A summer let, a school-year lease or a winter rental of a house or apartment is an ordinary tenancy under the landlord-tenant act, with the same deposit, repair, notice and eviction rules as any other. The act's only duration-based carve-out is for 'Transient occupancy in a hotel, motel or other similar lodgings' (Iowa Code § 562A.5(4)), and Iowa does not define transient for that purpose. The hotel and motel tax exempts lodging rented to the same person for more than 31 consecutive days (Iowa Code § 423A.5(1)(a); `edu-rent-tax-ia`), but that is a tax rule, not a test of who is a tenant. Treat anyone renting a dwelling as a home for a season as a tenant: put the exact start and end dates in a signed lease, take and return any deposit under the deposit rules, and if the occupant stays past the end date, recover possession only through the court (`edu-eviction-process-ia`, `edu-self-help-eviction-ia`). A written lease that fixes its end date ends on that date (Iowa Code § 562.6), but serving written notice at least 30 days before the last day is the cautious course (Iowa Code § 562A.34(3); `edu-end-of-term-ia`). Short stays of thirty days or less are short-term rental property for city zoning purposes, and a city 'shall not adopt or enforce any regulation, restriction, or other ordinance, including a conditional use permit requirement, relating to short-term rental properties within the city' (Iowa Code § 414.1(1)(e)(2)), apart from listed safety, nuisance and emergency-contact rules. Farm tenancies, which end on March 1, have their own rules (Iowa Code § 562.5) and are outside this library. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Changing Lease Terms in Iowa
bodyText:
Iowa has no statute on changing the terms of a tenancy in general.

Three rules decide what you can do. Rent: 'Each tenant shall be notified, in writing, of any rent increase at least thirty days before the effective date' (Iowa Code § 562A.13(5)), and the increase cannot take effect before the lease, or a renewal or extension of it, expires (`edu-rent-increase-notice-ia`). Iowa defines rent as 'a payment to be made to the landlord under the rental agreement' (Iowa Code § 562A.6(10)), so treat a higher fee, such as pet rent or a parking or utility charge, as a rent increase: the same 30 days' written notice, and no increase during a fixed term. No Iowa statute asks for a longer notice for fees.

Rules: you may adopt new written rules during the tenancy, and a new rule 'is enforceable against the tenant if reasonable notice of its adoption is given to the tenant and it does not work a substantial modification of the rental agreement' (Iowa Code § 562A.18(2); `rules-ia`).

Everything else: during a fixed term, other terms change only by a written agreement both of you sign. In a month-to-month tenancy, no statute lets a notice rewrite the lease by itself, so the safe route is to end the current tenancy and offer a new one on the changed terms: a written notice served at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in it (Iowa Code § 562A.34(2)), by signed acknowledgment, personal service, or posting plus regular and certified mail (Iowa Code § 562A.29A(1)), stating the new terms. The library offers an optional clause that builds this route into the lease: `term-change-notice-ia`.

A change that raises rent or cuts services soon after a tenant's code complaint, repair complaint or tenant-union activity can be challenged as retaliation (Iowa Code § 562A.36; `edu-retaliation-ia`).

Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: When a Tenant Files for Bankruptcy
bodyText: Iowa has no statute of its own on a tenant's bankruptcy. Its landlord-tenant act says only that the law of bankruptcy, with other principles of law and equity, supplements the act (Iowa Code § 562A.3). Federal bankruptcy law governs. In outline: a bankruptcy filing automatically stops (stays) lawsuits, collection of rent owed before the filing, and any act to obtain possession of the tenant's home (FEDERAL: 11 U.S.C. § 362(a)). Two exceptions matter to landlords. If you obtained a judgment for possession before the tenant filed, you may generally finish the eviction (FEDERAL: 11 U.S.C. § 362(b)(22)), but the tenant can delay that for 30 days by certifying a right to cure under state law and depositing rent with the bankruptcy court (FEDERAL: 11 U.S.C. § 362(l)). No Iowa statute read for this row gives a residential tenant a right to cure after a judgment for possession, but that question is for the bankruptcy court. An eviction based on the tenant endangering the property or illegal drug use on it can go forward after a certification you file and serve (FEDERAL: 11 U.S.C. § 362(b)(23), FEDERAL: 11 U.S.C. § 362(m)); Iowa's clear-and-present-danger eviction (`edu-clear-present-danger-ia`) does not by itself bring a case within that exception. A lease clause making bankruptcy or insolvency a default cannot be enforced after the filing (FEDERAL: 11 U.S.C. § 365(e)(1)), so the library's lease has none. In a Chapter 7 case an unassumed residential lease is treated as rejected after 60 days unless the court extends the time (FEDERAL: 11 U.S.C. § 365(d)(1)). Iowa law does not say whether a sheriff enforces a writ of possession after you learn of a filing. Cautious course: as soon as you learn a tenant has filed, stop any notice, eviction filing, lockout or collection of past rent, keep accepting current rent, and take advice before doing anything else. Administrative rules, case law and local ordinances were not searched, and the federal part is an outline only.

title: No Double-Letting Statute in Iowa
bodyText: Iowa has no double-letting statute: nothing specifically forbids letting part of a room to more than one family, and nothing gives other tenants a rent abatement when that happens. What Iowa does have covers the practical case of a unit promised to two tenants. 'At the commencement of the term, the landlord shall deliver possession of the premises to the tenant in compliance with the rental agreement and section 562A.15' (Iowa Code § 562A.14). If you do not, rent abates until possession is delivered, and the tenant may either end the lease on at least five days' written notice and get back all prepaid rent and the deposit, or demand performance and sue for possession against you or 'a person wrongfully in possession' (Iowa Code § 562A.22(1)(b)) and recover damages (Iowa Code § 562A.22(1)). If your failure is willful and not in good faith, the tenant also recovers actual damages and reasonable attorney fees (Iowa Code § 562A.22(2)). So never sign a second lease for a unit or room until the first one has ended, and if two people end up holding leases for the same space, tell both at once and offer the second a refund or another unit. Renting separate rooms in one dwelling to separate tenants is lawful, but each room is then its own dwelling unit, and a roomer who pays weekly rent with no fixed term has a week-to-week tenancy (Iowa Code § 562A.9(5)); occupancy limits in local housing codes may apply (`edu-rental-inspection-ia`). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Minors as Tenants and Eviction Defendants
bodyText: In Iowa 'The period of minority extends to the age of eighteen years, but all minors attain their majority by marriage' (Iowa Code § 599.1(1)). A juvenile court may also emancipate a minor of sixteen or older (Iowa Code § 232C.1(1)); the order gives the minor, among other things, 'The right to enter into a binding contract' (Iowa Code § 232C.4(1)(b)) and the ability to sue or be sued in the minor's own name (Iowa Code § 232C.4(1)(a)). A minor can sign a lease, but it is voidable: a minor is bound by contracts 'unless the minor disaffirms them within a reasonable time after attaining majority' (Iowa Code § 599.2) and returns what the minor received and still controls. The minor cannot disaffirm if the minor's own misrepresentation of age, or the minor's having engaged in business as an adult, gave you good reason to believe the minor could contract (Iowa Code § 599.3). Contracts for necessaries bind a minor without that escape (Iowa Code § 599.2); whether a lease is a necessary depends on the facts and on case law not read for this library. So check the age of every applicant who will sign, ask a minor for an emancipation order or marriage record, and otherwise have an adult sign as co-tenant or guarantor (`edu-guarantor-renewal-ia`). No Iowa statute bars an eviction filing against a minor or says which occupants must be named. Name and serve every tenant who signed the lease. Iowa's notice statutes let a resident 'at least eighteen years of age' sign for delivery of a termination notice or notice to quit (Iowa Code § 562A.29A(1)(a), Iowa Code § 648.3(2)(a)), so do not hand notices to a minor for that purpose. How a minor defendant is served and represented in court is governed by the Iowa Rules of Civil Procedure, which were not read for this row; if a tenant you must sue is under eighteen, take advice before filing.

title: Who Can Represent an Entity Landlord in Court
bodyText: Small claims court. Most Iowa evictions and many rent claims are small claims: an eviction on the usual grounds may be filed as a small claim (Iowa Code § 631.1(2)), and money claims of $6,500 or less are small claims (Iowa Code § 631.1(1)(b)). There, 'In actions in which a person other than an individual is a party, that person may be represented by an officer or an employee' (Iowa Code § 631.14(1)). So an LLC or corporation landlord can appear through its own officer or employee without a lawyer. If the rental is titled in the name of one or more individuals, an employee of an owner, or an officer or employee of a property management company acting for the owners, may bring the case in the owners' names, the management company's name or the name the property is commonly known by (Iowa Code § 631.14(2)(a)). That second rule covers only individually titled property: a management company that is not the entity owner's own officer or employee should not appear for an entity owner without a lawyer. A wrongly named landlord or tenant is corrected by substituting the real party, not by dismissal (Iowa Code § 631.14(2)(b)). To file electronically, a nonlawyer appearing for an entity or an individual owner registers as a filing agent (Iowa Ct. R. 16.304). Other courts. No statute lets a nonlawyer appear for an entity outside small claims, for example in a district court eviction not filed as a small claim, a larger damages claim, or an appeal. Whether an entity must use a lawyer there is governed by court rules and case law not read for this row, so hire a lawyer. Out-of-state entities. 'A foreign limited liability company doing business in this state shall not maintain a proceeding in any court of this state until it is registered to do business in this state' (Iowa Code § 489.902(2)); foreign corporations, limited partnerships, limited liability partnerships and nonprofit corporations face the same bar (Iowa Code § 490.1502(2), Iowa Code § 488.907(2), Iowa Code § 486A.1103(1), Iowa Code § 504.1502(1)). Owning, protecting and maintaining property is not by itself doing business (Iowa Code § 489.905(1)(j), Iowa Code § 490.1505(1)(j)), but whether renting homes to tenants is has not been settled in any authority read here, so register before you file. An unregistered company's leases stay valid and it may still defend a suit (Iowa Code § 489.902(3)). Trade names. An individual who rents under a business name other than the owners' true surnames must first record a verified statement with the county recorder (Iowa Code § 547.1); breaking that rule is a simple misdemeanor for each day (Iowa Code § 547.4, Iowa Code § 547.5), but Iowa's trade-name chapter does not bar a suit. Limited partnerships, limited liability companies, corporations, cooperatives and nonprofit corporations organized in Iowa or registered here are exempt (Iowa Code § 547.1); other persons, including a general partnership, are not. Being sued. You must disclose to the tenant in writing, at or before the start of the tenancy (the lease is the usual place), the name and address of an owner or agent for service of process (Iowa Code § 562A.13(1)(b); `landlord-disclosure-ia`); if you do not, your manager becomes your agent for service (Iowa Code § 562A.13(3)). A nonresident who contracts with an Iowa resident can be served through the Iowa secretary of state (Iowa Code § 617.3(2)-(3)).

title: Barring Non-Tenants Under the Trespass Law
bodyText: Iowa's general criminal trespass statute lets you keep a non-tenant off the common areas you control. Trespass includes 'Entering or remaining upon or in property without justification after being notified or requested to abstain from entering or to remove or vacate therefrom by the owner, lessee, or person in lawful possession, or the agent or employee of the owner' (Iowa Code § 716.7(2)(a)(2)). The notice can be given to the person 'personally, either orally or in writing' (Iowa Code § 716.7(2)(a)(2)(a)), or by a printed or written notice 'conspicuously posted or exhibited at the main entrance to the property or the forbidden part of the property' (Iowa Code § 716.7(2)(a)(2)(b)). A knowing trespass is a simple misdemeanor, and a serious misdemeanor if it injures someone or causes more than $300 of damage (Iowa Code § 716.8(1)-(2)). Practical course: give the person a dated written notice naming the property and the parts they may not enter, keep a copy, and call the police if they return. Three limits. First, you cannot use a trespass notice against your own tenant to get them out: removing or excluding a tenant without a court order is unlawful (Iowa Code § 562A.26; `edu-self-help-eviction-ia`). Second, a tenant is a lessee in lawful possession of the unit and may invite guests to it, and the statute reaches only a person who stays 'without justification' (Iowa Code § 716.7(2)(a)(2)); whether your ban overrides a tenant's invitation to the unit itself is not settled by any statute (no guest or invitee rule exists) and turns on case law not read here. Base any ban on the person's conduct, apply it to common areas, and enforce your guest rules against the tenant through the lease (`guest-policy-ia`, `rules-ia`; noncompliance notice, `edu-noncompliance-cure-ia`). Third, a ban must not rest on a protected characteristic (`edu-fair-housing-ia`) or punish a call for police or emergency help (`edu-emergency-assistance-ia`). For a person who endangers others, the tenant can avoid a clear-and-present-danger termination by, among other steps, writing to the person 'telling the person not to return to the premises and that a return to the premises may result in a trespass or other action against the person' (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(3)(a)(3)) and copying the police; see `edu-clear-present-danger-ia`.

title: No Pet Eviction Fact Sheet in Iowa
bodyText: Iowa has no pet-and-eviction fact sheet, and no rule that you give a tenant with a dog or cat any notice about pets when you sign the lease or start an eviction. Iowa's landlord-tenant act does not mention animals at all; your pet terms come from the lease (`pet-policy-ia`, `edu-pet-deposit-ia`), and assistance animals follow the fair housing rules (`edu-assistance-animals-ia`). The rule that matters at move-out is criminal and binds the owner of the animal: 'A person commits animal abandonment if the person owns or has custody of a cat or dog and relinquishes all rights in and duties to care for the cat or dog' (Iowa Code § 717B.8(1)); handing the animal to someone who accepts it, or to an authorized shelter or pound, is not abandonment (Iowa Code § 717B.8(2)(a)-(b)). So when you serve a notice to quit or file for possession, tell the tenant in writing to take every pet when they leave. If an animal is left behind after the tenant has gone or the court has restored possession to you, do not treat it like furniture under the left-property clause (`abandoned-property-ia`): give it water and food, contact the tenant at once, and if they do not collect it promptly, call local animal control or an authorized shelter. Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: No Foreclosure Disclosure Duty in Iowa
bodyText: No Iowa statute requires you to tell a new or existing tenant that the rental is in foreclosure, or that you have received a foreclosure petition or notice. The Iowa disclosures that every lease needs are listed in `edu-required-disclosures-ia`; foreclosure is not among them. Two things still argue for telling an applicant before signing. First, a foreclosure can end the tenancy: a person who stays after a foreclosure sale can be removed by forcible entry and detainer (Iowa Code § 648.1(4); `edu-no-foreclosure-tenant-rule-ia`), and federal law gives bona fide tenants notice rights against the new owner (`edu-ptfa-foreclosure-tenants`). Second, Iowa's landlord-tenant act is supplemented by the general law of fraud and misrepresentation (Iowa Code § 562A.3), and leasing practices can fall under the consumer fraud law (`edu-consumer-protection-ia`); hiding a pending foreclosure from someone about to pay rent and a deposit invites a claim that no statute rules out. Cautious course: if a foreclosure is pending, say so in writing before the applicant signs or pays, and keep the deposit records current so they pass to a successor (`edu-deposit-on-sale-ia`, `edu-sale-management-change-ia`). Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: When the Property Is Taken by Eminent Domain
bodyText:
No Iowa statute says what a taking by eminent domain does to a residential lease. Nothing ends or reduces the rent, lets the court cancel the lease, makes the statute defer to the lease, or lets you and the tenant file an agreement dividing the award. The commissioners assess 'the damages which the owner will sustain by reason of the appropriation' (Iowa Code § 6B.14(1)), and title passes to the condemner when damages are finally determined and paid (Iowa Code § 6B.25(1)(d)). How that money is shared between you and a tenant, and when the rent stops, is left to the lease and to case law.

So if your rental could be taken, say it in the lease. The library's optional Condemnation clause (`eminent-domain-vi`) ends the lease on a total taking, reduces rent on a partial one, keeps the award for you except the tenant's own relocation and personal-property payments, and returns the deposit as the lease provides.

Tenants have rights of their own in the proceeding, which no lease can take away. The condemner must send notice of the proposed acquisition 'to any tenant known to be occupying the property' (Iowa Code § 6B.2D(1)), except on some street, highway and utility projects (Iowa Code § 6B.2D(2)), and must mail or serve the condemnation application on that tenant (Iowa Code § 6B.3(2)). A tenant occupying under a recorded lease may sue to challenge the taking (Iowa Code § 6A.24(1)). To the greatest extent practicable no one lawfully occupying a dwelling must move on less than ninety days' written notice (Iowa Code § 6B.54(4)), and a displaced tenant can receive a replacement-housing payment from the displacing agency (Iowa Code § 316.6).

Keep collecting rent until the tenant must leave, unless your lease says otherwise, and refund rent paid for later days.

Manufactured home community lots are governed by Iowa Code ch. 562B, not covered here.

title: Notices About Proceedings Against the Property
bodyText: No Iowa statute makes you tell your tenants about a lawsuit, foreclosure, tax sale, condemnation or other proceeding against the property, and none makes a tenant who is served with papers about the property tell you. Both gaps are filled another way. Tenants often hear directly: a mortgagee foreclosing without a court must serve its notice 'on the person in possession of the real estate, if different than the mortgagor' (Iowa Code § 655A.3(2)); a tax-sale buyer serves the notice that the right of redemption will expire on 'the person in possession of the parcel' (Iowa Code § 447.9(1)); and in a condemnation the condemner notifies 'any tenant known to be occupying the property' (Iowa Code § 6B.2D(1); `edu-eminent-domain-ia`). For foreclosure disclosure to new tenants see `edu-no-foreclosure-disclosure-ia`. To learn of proceedings yourself, rely on the lease: the library's clause requiring the tenant to tell you at once and hand over any written notice of a proceeding to recover the property is already part of the Iowa lease (`tenant-forward-proceedings-ca`). And a tenant cannot switch sides: rent paid, or possession delivered, to anyone but you 'is void, and shall not affect the rights of such lessor' (Iowa Code § 562.3) unless you consented or a judgment, decree or judicial sale to which you were a party required it. If someone sues your tenant to recover the property and the tenant is only a tenant, you may be substituted as defendant, and the judgment then binds you (Iowa Code § 646.11).
